messages.author: 5270e62a7d3ec577
messages.subject: Re: Activity data output
parts:
Hi Lisa,

You can use "epochvalues2csv = TRUE" in your script to generate csv files containing epoch level data. 
As long as you specified windowsizes = c(60,900,3600) then you would get 60s epoch files with a 15 min non-wear detection resolution and 60 min non-wear evaluation window

Kind regards,
Ben

messages.author: 5270e62a7d3ec577
messages.subject: Re: Activity data output
parts:
Hi Lisa,

bodylocation simply generates the column in the summary files as a log to inform the user where the device was worn, and this only works if you actually specify this in the software when setting this up. If you don't specify the wear site you still get all the same data but bodylocation will state "not extracted" on each row. 

You would need to read around the comparability of data when worn on chest vs wrist, and treat the output data accordingly - This won't be done in GGIR. I have only used accelerometers on thigh, wrist and waist so I'm afraid I can't really help, but someone else may chip in here if they know of any literature that might help guide your interpretation.

Kind regards,
Ben

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Activity data output
parts:
In addition to Ben's response it may be good to clarify that:

- Default sleep detection approach is optimized for wrist, possibly the algorithm also works for other body locations with some tweaking of parameters, but there is no literature yet on the validity of that.
- Time spent in inactivity, light, moderate or vigorous physical activity is done based on thresholds. The defaults are set for wrist, but you as user can modify them as you wish and tailor them to other attachment locations. I put some guidance here.
- All other output variables are basic descriptors of the data, and should be interpreted with the attachment location in mind.
- Non-wear detection should work across attachment locations, since not wearing an accelerometer is by definition not attachment specific.
- Auto-calibration success might be challenged, but part 2 csv report will always tell you whether it had difficulty reducing the calibration error. If it is a problem then you may want to consider doing separate calibration experiments and use the calibration correction coefficients from those as input (see documentation for backup.cal.coef) 

Best,
Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant
https://accelting.com/

messages.subject: Re: Activity data output
parts:
Hi Gabriela,
I'm not sure of what you mean by your first question. If you are asking about how to get the ID within column A in the outputs (e.g. part2_daysummary.cs) then you can specify idloc = 2 in the g.shell function. If you just want a column within the csv file to specify the ID, then you would be looking at writing a simple batch loop in R or other software to carry this out.
It's been a while since I generated the csv epoch data, I'm pretty sure it's post-calibration, but includes all the data regardless of nonwear. I could very well be wrong though and happy to be corrected.
Ben

messages.author: bbe16334c21daa24
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Activity data output
parts:
Hello All,

My interpretation reading this is that what is happening is that during part2, each short epoch value (e.g. 5 s) — which is what you have output in the epochvalues2csv file — must be estimated from the all the raw data (which might be up to 100 Hz) in that window. In other words, I think GGIR has to determine if that 5s epoch is going to be a zero (thus classified as non-wear) or as some other value above zero (thus valid wear). So, I think there is some estimation (imputation), using a sliding overlapping or non-overlapping window (depending on your short, medium, and long epoch lengths) of whether the data within each 5s epoch are valid (i.e. >0) or invalid (=0).

Anyone else know if this interpretation is correct?

Graydon

El vie, 30 abr 2021 a las 15:07, ben_m...@hotmail.com (<ben_m...@hotmail.com>) escribió:
Hi Gabriela,
I'm not sure of what you mean by your first question. If you are asking about how to get the ID within column A in the outputs (e.g. part2_daysummary.cs) then you can specify idloc = 2 in the g.shell function. If you just want a column within the csv file to specify the ID, then you would be looking at writing a simple batch loop in R or other software to carry this out.
It's been a while since I generated the csv epoch data, I'm pretty sure it's post-calibration, but includes all the data regardless of nonwear. I could very well be wrong though and happy to be corrected.
Ben

Hello Ben and Lisa,
Do you know if the csv output can be obtained with the id_file in a column? I am procesing varius files and can not find a way to identify them i  the output. Also, do you know if this output is after calibration and elimination of nonwear time? 
Thank you very much
El martes, 2 de febrero de 2021 a las 11:25:16 UTC+1, ben_m...@hotmail.com escribió:
Hi Lisa,

You can use "epochvalues2csv = TRUE" in your script to generate csv files containing epoch level data. 
As long as you specified windowsizes = c(60,900,3600) then you would get 60s epoch files with a 15 min non-wear detection resolution and 60 min non-wear evaluation window
Kind regards,
Ben

Hi Lisa,

Oh, I now see, nobody responded to your message...
Yes you can do that with GGIR:
- See argument "epochvalues2csv" for exporting part 2 output.
- See argument "save_ms5rawlevels" for exporting part 5 time series.
- Also, it may be god to know that a lot of the intermediate output for each part is stored in the .RData files in the output folder.

Best, Vincent
